recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future changes should only be considered if Pharmacy reopens the later DetectedIssue design; any clarification should live in Medication Module or DetectedIssue retrieval guidance rather than on removed MedicationRequest.detectedIssue or MedicationDispense.detectedIssue elements.
issue_request: FHIR-13150 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and requested additional description or definition guidance explaining what information MedicationRequest.detectedIssue and MedicationDispense.detectedIssue conveyed and how they could be used.
initial_application: The Jira comment links applied commit ccfc10c2b0d8324e7805bdad3489470709201430. That commit added comments to the then-current MedicationRequest.detectedIssue and MedicationDispense.detectedIssue spreadsheet rows explaining that detected issues could be identified by decision support systems or clinicians and could include mitigation steps.
additional_context: Later Published issue FHIR-34293 removed MedicationRequest.detectedIssue and MedicationDispense.detectedIssue because DetectedIssue already points to implicated therapies and FHIR references are not bidirectional. Commit 26e2a82259 removed the direct elements, and combined-branch commit e25b1231a9ed3c4fec8abcdec9281d95a66dd10c added the current Medication Module guidance for DetectedIssue.implicated searches, _revinclude, and containment. FHIR-39018 later reaffirmed the same non-bidirectional design.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit for FHIR-13150. Reintroducing local element comments or direct medication-to-DetectedIssue references would conflict with the later current-spec Pharmacy decision, and the current replacement guidance is already present on the combined branch.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive with Modification issue removed the direct MedicationRequest.detectedIssue and MedicationDispense.detectedIssue elements and required replacement Medication Module guidance.
